If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

That habit of planning and foreseeing potential hiccups can spill over into other areas—career decisions, financial planning, even personal relationships. Repeated exposure to small crises builds a kind of “stress inoculation.” You learn to stay calm, find creative solutions, and bounce back. That resilience can translate into a more optimistic outlook on life’s bigger uncertainties. ### 3. **Empathy and Perspective** Caring for others—especially children—naturally expands your empathy. You become attuned to subtle cues, needs, and emotions that you might otherwise overlook. Over time, this heightened sensitivity can make you more compassionate in your professional life, in friendships, and even in your own self‑care. ### 4. **Prioritization and Value Clarification** Deciding what to cook, what to schedule, and what to let go of forces you to clarify what truly matters. You learn to weigh options quickly and make trade‑offs. This skill can help you set long‑term goals that align with your core values, rather than getting lost in the noise of everyday demands. ### 5. **Time‑Management as a Life Skill** The “time‑boxing” you use for meals and appointments becomes a framework for any project.
